_doc: Indicator registry for the Danish makro view. `db` = '' (Statistics Denmark), 's20' (Finans Danmark) or 's30' (Copenhagen). `level` = finest geography the indicator natively exists at. `calc` describes the post-processing in build_makro.py. `hue` = RGB target for the choropleth ramp (paper #EFF2EE → hue). `pull` names a raw file when one table is fetched with several selections. `SUM` = omit the variable so the API returns its total. `TODO:word` = placeholder; validate_config.py lists codes whose label contains the word. `direction` = 'higher_better' | 'lower_better' — which end of the scale is favourable (ranking and good/bad colouring). `note` = glossary text for the indicator's details. `chip` = true puts the indicator in the quick-pick chip row. Rolling-quarter calcs (Safety): `rolling4q_per_1000_pop` = sum of the numerator over the latest 4 quarters ÷ FOLK1A population at the same end quarter × 1000; `rolling4q_per_1000_dwellings` = same sum ÷ BOL101 dwellings of the latest year × 1000; `rolling4q_yoy_pct` = latest 4Q sum vs the 4 quarters before, %. For the yearly history each calendar year is filed as its Q1–Q4 sum (÷ population at Q4); the live value is the rolling 4Q ending at the latest quarter. A `select` value may be a list of codes (rows matching any of them are summed). `history_from` = first year of the yearly history (Charts axis; default: history_years back from the latest year); `map_from` = first year offered by the map/table year selector, and the start of the quarterly rolling series; `breaks` = series breaks drawn in Charts, [{at: '2013K3' | '2023', text}]. `note_short` = the one caveat worth repeating in a map popup (the full `note` stays in the ⓘ details). `calc: infra_index` reads data/processed/infra_index.json (scripts/build_infra.py) instead of a StatBank pull. `calc: public_index` reads data/processed/public_index.json (scripts/build_public.py).

indicators.label: Reported crime · per 1,000 inh.
indicators.desc: Penal-code offences (straffelov i alt) reported in the municipality over the latest 4 quarters, per 1,000 inhabitants.
indicators.source: DST STRAF11 (reported offences by place of offence, quarterly) · FOLK1A
indicators.note: Denominator is resident population. City-centre areas with heavy daytime and night-time footfall (tourists, shopping, nightlife) score high because offences such as theft from person happen there, not because residents are unsafe — compare with Feeling safe (%), which is 90 % in Indre By. Place of offence (gerningskommune). Reported offences — reported ≠ solved. Excludes the traffic law. Series breaks: 2007 (police reform), 1 July 2013 (new definition of sexual offences), 2023 (~1,700 animal-welfare reports missing nationally). Not seasonally adjusted — hence rolling 4 quarters.

breaks.text: 1 July 2013: Criminal Code amendments on sexual offences (more offences classed as rape, §216) — series break in the penal-code total (DST footnote, STRAF11/STRAF22).

indicators.warn: An open case in BBR is owner-reported and is not a confirmed construction schedule: in the pilot only 1 of 290 open cases carried an expected completion date, and the median permit was 4.1 years old in København. Read it as case activity, not as a construction pipeline.
indicators.note: Counts only cases with a permit (or case) date within the last three years; older open cases are listed separately in the area panel. Pilot coverage as for public_m2_per_1000.
indicators.source: BBR via Datafordeler (bygningens anvendelse 410–449), addresses and missing coordinates from DAR — see docs/PUBLIC_BUILDINGS.md

indicators.label: FP9 grade average
indicators.desc: Weighted average of the bundne prøver at Folkeskolens Afgangseksamen (9th grade), latest school year, pupil-weighted over the schools of the area.
indicators.warn: A grade average is not a quality ranking — it mostly tracks intake. Read it next to the socioeconomic reference difference, which is what the source publishes it for.
indicators.note: Pupil-weighted over folkeskoler and frie grundskoler that have a value; specialskoler are excluded because their intake makes an average meaningless. A school whose cell the source suppressed (under 3 observations, under 5 pupils for trivsel and the socioøkonomisk reference) is absent from the mean, not counted as zero — so an area's figure covers only the schools that publish. Copenhagen metro set only (19 municipalities).
indicators.note_short: FP9 bundne prøver, pupil-weighted; specialskoler excluded
indicators.source: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk (STIL) — GS cubes KARA/KARAGNS (grades), OVER/OVERSKO (socioøkonomisk reference, klassekvotient), TRIV/TRIVIND (trivsel), ELEV/ELEVEX (elevtal); STIL institutionsregister for location and type. Kilde: Uddannelsesstatistik.dk — see docs/SCHOOLS.md

indicators.label: Grade vs socioeconomic reference
indicators.desc: Difference between the schools' actual FP9 grade average and the socioeconomic reference — the grade the ministry's model expects given the pupils' background. Positive means the schools do better than their intake predicts.
indicators.warn: The difference is a model residual, not a causal claim about teaching. STIL marks per school whether it is statistically significant; most schools sit within the uncertainty band.
indicators.note: Pupil-weighted over folkeskoler and frie grundskoler that have a value; specialskoler are excluded because their intake makes an average meaningless. Copenhagen metro set only (19 municipalities). Published one year behind the grades, so the latest school year usually has grades but no reference yet.
indicators.note_short: actual minus expected FP9 grade, pupil-weighted

forecast._doc: Outlook group — DST's municipal population projection, built by scripts/build_forecast.py into data/processed/forecast.json and checked by scripts/validate_forecast.py. Held under its own top-level key rather than in `indicators[]` because `calc: forecast` and `db: forecast` are not yet implemented: build_makro.py would fall through to a StatBank raw-file lookup and raise FileNotFoundError. Phase B moves these entries into `indicators[]` once build_makro.py, and app.js's colour model, understand them (see docs/FORECAST.md, Phase B notes). Entries are looked up by `key` — `indicators()` in scripts/build_forecast.py returns one dict per kommune keyed by exactly these keys — and `field` names the underlying field the value is derived from. `calc: housing_gap` / `db: housing_gap` is the second Outlook source: data/processed/housing_gap.json from scripts/build_housing_gap.py, which compares the households the projection's five-year growth implies — household size carried forward on a capped trend — against the recent net change in the dwelling stock; it is inert here for the same reason. Its two entries differ only by `field`, so the Phase B branch must read `field` rather than hard-code one name: `fc_hh_gap_rel` (gap_per_1000_rel, measured against Denmark) is the one meant for the map and is listed first, `fc_hh_gap` (gap_per_1000) carries the level. `scale: diverging` with `center: 0` asks for a two-ended ramp from `hue_neg` through the paper tint to `hue_pos`, with class breaks symmetric about the centre — the existing renderer only does the single-ended `hue` ramp with quintile breaks, which is why `hue` is kept as the positive end. `direction: neutral` means neither end is 'better': shrinking is not failure and growth is not success, so these must not be ranked or coloured good/bad.

indicators.warn: A projection, not a measurement. DST's municipal projection assumes each municipality's recent fertility, mortality and migration behaviour continues; it carries no housing programme, so a large planned development does not appear in it.
indicators.note: Computed in scripts/build_forecast.py from data/processed/forecast.json: the 2026 vintage of DST's municipal projection, ages folded into 0–5, 6–16, 17–19, 20–34, 35–64, 65–79 and 80+. Christiansø (411) is not a municipality and has no value. Never read together with Københavns Kommune's own forecast, which is a different run — see docs/FORECAST.md.

Denmark's own 20–34 population falls 7.1 % over the window, so only 7 of 98 municipalities gain any at all and the absolute map is almost uniformly negative; this one shows who holds young adults better or worse than the country.

indicators.label: Housing gap vs Denmark, next 5 yrs
indicators.desc: The municipality's housing gap per 1 000 inhabitants minus Denmark's. Positive = the household growth the 2026→2031 projection implies outruns the recent pace of net dwelling additions by more than it does nationally — a tighter market than the country; negative = looser. Every municipality is negative in absolute terms, so this is the version that reads as a map.
indicators.source: Danmarks Statistik FOLK1A (population), FAM55N (households), BOL101 (dwelling stock) and FRKM126 (2026 municipal population projection) — see docs/FORECAST.md §7
indicators.warn: Measured against Denmark, not against zero: a positive value means tighter than the country, not undersupplied. An arithmetic comparison, not a housing-market forecast: household size is carried forward on a capped linear trend, the building pace is the flat 2020–2026 net stock change, and DST's projection is itself not housing-driven, so neither side responds to the other. A backtest of the same formula on 2020→2025 ranks municipalities no better than the simpler version it replaced.
indicators.note: Computed in scripts/build_housing_gap.py into data/processed/housing_gap.json. persons_per_hh is the municipality's own FOLK1A population ÷ FAM55N households at 1 January, read for six years and carried forward at its mean yearly change, with the total five-year move capped at ±5 % and floored at 1.6 persons; demand_5y = P2031 / persons_per_hh_2031 − P2026 / persons_per_hh_2026, i.e. the households the projection implies rather than the people; supply_5y = the change in the BOL101 dwelling stock 2020→2026 annualised over its six years × 5, which nets demolitions, mergers and conversions off (BOL101 publishes no 2021 or 2022, both closed by DST); gap = demand_5y − supply_5y and the per-1 000 figure is gap ÷ P2026 × 1000. Direction is neutral and the indicator must not be ranked good-to-bad — but for an owner a tighter market is supportive for rents and a looser one is not. housing_gap.json stores every component, both superseded variants (constant household size, gross BYGV33 completions) and the permitted-not-started pipeline as context; none of the context fields enters the figure. Vacancy, second homes and student housing are not modelled, and where the projection shrinks demand_5y is negative, so any net additions read as oversupply. This indicator subtracts Denmark's own gap_per_1000 of −13.9, where Denmark is the sum of the same 98 municipalities computed the same way, not a separately averaged national ratio (scripts/validate_forecast.py check 6 asserts both the identity and the sum). That puts 41 of 98 municipalities above the line and 57 below, against 0 of 98 on the absolute version. The two ends mean different things and the popup must show demand_5y alongside the gap: at the top are built-out municipalities whose projected household growth nearly matches their net additions, at the bottom a mix of shrinking municipalities, where demand_5y is negative and any building reads as oversupply, and fast-building growth municipalities such as Høje-Taastrup. Christiansø (411) is not a municipality and has no value.
indicators.note_short: Measured against Denmark's own −13.9 per 1 000, not against zero — all 98 municipalities are negative in absolute terms, so a positive value means tighter than the country, not undersupplied.

indicators.label: Housing gap next 5 yrs, dwellings per 1,000 inh.

Positive = undersupply. All 98 municipalities are negative in this vintage — for a map use the vs-Denmark version, fc_hh_gap_rel.
